## The frame {#frame .lund-part data-part="0"}

::: {.lund-big}
For the next ten years, the social contract still holds.
:::

Universities **certify**: a degree says the candidate passed the exams.
Knowledge is **chunked**:

::: {.lund-nest}
::: {.lund-box}
**Study programme**

::: {.lund-box}
**Course**

::: {.lund-box}
**Topic**

[Definition]{.lund-chip} [Notation]{.lund-chip} [Example]{.lund-chip} [Method]{.lund-chip} [Exercise]{.lund-chip}
:::
:::
:::
:::

AI or not, these lower-level chunks will most likely survive.

::: {.lund-cols}
::: {.lund-card .lund-inside}
### Inside the course

What we chose: this notation, these examples, these methods, and what is assessed.
:::

::: {.lund-card .lund-outside}
### Outside the course

Everything else: other books, other conventions, other levels.
:::
:::

::: {.lund-cols .lund-derivatives}
::: {.lund-card}
$$\frac{d}{dx}\,\sqrt{x^2+1}$$
:::

::: {.lund-card}
$$\frac{d}{dx}\,\sqrt{x+\sqrt{x+\sqrt{x+\sqrt{x}}}}$$
:::
:::

::: {.lund-question}
The lecturer feels which one belongs. **Does the model?**
:::

## Retrieval-Augmented Generation {#rag .lund-part data-part="2"}

::: {.lund-big}
One way to define the course for a model: let it read the course.
:::

The simplest way: upload the course PDF to a chat. It works, more or less.

::: {.lund-problems}
::: {.lund-problem}
**Soup**\
formulas and figures get lost on the way ([3b](#pdf))
:::
::: {.lund-problem}
**A frozen copy**\
change the course, and every uploaded copy is out of date
:::
::: {.lund-problem}
**Inside and outside mixed**\
nothing shows where the PDF ends and the model's own knowledge begins
:::
::: {.lund-problem}
**Somebody else's server**\
every question goes to a commercial provider
:::
:::

RAG: look up first, then answer. Answer A in [1b](#one-button) did this by hand.

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 9
%%{init: {"themeVariables": {"fontSize": "18px"}}}%%
flowchart LR
  S([Student asks]) --> L["Retrieve<br/>a librarian finds the right passages"]
  L -->|"Augment: passages + question"| M["Generate<br/>the model answers, course first"]
  M --> A([Answer])
  C[(The course,<br/>in short passages)] --- L
  classDef course fill:#fff8ec,stroke:#e8a33d
  classDef model fill:#eaf6ee,stroke:#2e8b57
  classDef student fill:#eef5fd,stroke:#2780e3
  class C,L course
  class M model
  class S,A student
```

### What lives where

::: {.lund-where}
::: {.lund-place .is-github}
**The course pages**\
where the teacher writes them: GitHub
:::
::: {.lund-place .is-server}
**The librarian and the passages**\
a small server at NTNU; updated whenever the course changes
:::
::: {.lund-place .is-cluster}
**The language model**\
NTNU's large computing cluster; nothing leaves NTNU
:::
::: {.lund-place .is-browser}
**The student**\
only a web browser
:::
:::

::: {.lund-question}
**Inside first**: the answer comes from the course passages.
**Outside if needed**: anything else comes after, clearly labelled.
:::

Our RAG service: ask a question about one course.

## What it is, and how it looks {#source .lund-part data-part="3a"}

::: {.lund-big}
Write what the mathematics **is**. Let the tools decide how it **looks**.
:::

::: {.lund-cols .lund-data}
::: {.lund-card .lund-data-source}
#### Plain text (Markdown): what the lecturer writes

````markdown
```{math-exercise}
#| label: lund-derivative-course
#| caption: From the course (part 1)
#| vars: x
#| context: none
#| similar: true
#| harder: Combine the chain rule with a product or a quotient, keeping the function short.
#| simpler: Use a single power of a linear expression.
Differentiate $f(x)=\sqrt{x^2+1}$. $f'(x)=$ __[x/sqrt(x^2+1)]
```
````

A few lines: the task, the answer, what "harder" means. Nothing about how it looks.
:::

::: {.lund-card .lund-data-html}
#### HTML: what the browser gets

::: {#lund-html-monster}
:::

Messy, huge, never written by hand. Rendered, it looks good:
the exercise in [part 5](#practice).
:::
:::

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 9
%%{init: {"themeVariables": {"fontSize": "18px"}}}%%
flowchart LR
  T(["Lecturers"]) --> Q["The course, as plain text<br/>text · mathematics · code"]
  Q --> W(["Website<br/>for students"])
  Q --> P(["Passages<br/>for the RAG service"])
  Q --> E(["Printed matter"])
  classDef people fill:#eef5fd,stroke:#2780e3
  classDef source fill:#f3f0fa,stroke:#6f42c1
  class T,W,P,E people
  class Q source
```

::: {.lund-question}
Written once, as plain text. The website, the RAG service and printed matter are views of it.
There is no AI version of the course.
:::

## PDF: only the looks {#pdf .lund-part .lund-sub data-part="3b"}

::: {.lund-big}
A PDF keeps how the page looks, and loses what it is.
:::

Copy the text out of a PDF of our physics exercises:

::: {.lund-soup}
| On the page | Copied out of the PDF | In our plain text |
|---|---|---|
| $3{,}93\cdot10^{26}\,\mathrm{W}$ | `3,93 ⋅ 1026 W` | `$3{,}93\cdot10^{26}\,\mathrm{W}$` |
| $4{,}50\cdot10^{23}$ molekyler | `4,50 ⋅ 1023 molekyler` | `$4{,}50\cdot10^{23}$ molekyler` |
| $U_1=150\,\mathrm{V}$ | `𝑈𝑈1 = 150 V` | `$U_1=150\,\mathrm{V}$` |
| the figure | *(nothing)* | `![A ball against a spring](oppgave4.png)` |
:::

The power of a star became 1026 watts: one microwave oven.

::: {.lund-question}
Special models guess the structure back, and still get the mathematics wrong.
Start from plain text, and there is nothing to guess.
:::

## Many lecturers, one course {#lecturers .lund-part .lund-sub data-part="3c"}

::: {.lund-big}
Because it is plain text, every change is saved, read before it goes live, and can be undone.
:::

::: {.lund-history}
- [Lecturer A]{.who} changes the vector notation in week 3
- [Lecturer B]{.who} adds an exercise on eigenvalues
- [Lecturer C]{.who} reads both changes and approves them
- [Published]{.who .is-done} both go live
:::

[In GitHub's words: commits, pull requests, history.]{.lund-small}

::: {.lund-question}
Fix it once: a corrected sign reaches the website and the RAG service together.
:::

## Open source {#open-source .lund-part .lund-sub data-part="3d"}

::: {.lund-big}
The text lasts; the views change. The course belongs to its lecturers, not to a platform.
:::

::::: {.lund-steps}
::: {.lund-step}
**Any server**\
GitHub today, another place tomorrow
:::
::: {.lund-step}
**Plain text files**\
readable in ten years, by any tool and any model
:::
::: {.lund-step}
**Share and reuse**\
between courses and between universities
:::
:::::

[Free, open-source tools: Quarto, Pyodide, CTM Assessment.]{.lund-small}

## Assessment: deterministic and stochastic {#assessment .lund-part data-part="4a"}

::: {.lund-big}
What students do has to be assessed.
:::

::: {.lund-question}
But any written product made at home is no longer authentic: a model may have written it.
The text alone no longer shows who did the thinking.
:::

So we split the work:

::::: {.lund-steps}
::: {.lund-step}
**Small chunks**\
basic skills, practised one by one, with immediate feedback
:::
::: {.lund-step}
**Larger projects**\
skills combined; any tool, AI included; but students explain their work, to each other or to us
:::
:::::

Here: the core skills. Online, this is **formative**: it helps students through a constructive struggle.

::: {.lund-cols}
::: {.lund-card .lund-inside}
### Deterministic: the check

The same answer gives the same result, every time.
:::

::: {.lund-card .lund-outside}
### Stochastic: the AI

Reads the task, the student's work and the teacher's prompt ([4c](#prompts)),
then suggests the next step. It can vary, and it can be wrong.
:::
:::

::: {.lund-question}
The check decides whether the answer is right. The AI helps with the way there.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Paper and typed {#paper .lund-part .lund-sub data-part="4b"}

The ball problem from the tab above, twice:

::: {.lund-cols .lund-paper}
::: {.lund-card}
#### On paper: how students think

![](assets/handskrift/student1/1a.png){fig-alt="A student's handwritten solution: a ball thrown up from 1.5 m at 6.0 m/s. The student finds the extra height 1.83 m, the total height 3.3 m and the time 0.6 s, with units throughout."}
:::

::: {.lund-card}
#### Typed: what the machine checks

```text
t = 0.61
h = 3.3
```

No units, no formula, no steps: only the numbers.
:::
:::

::: {.lund-big}
The check needs it typed. Language models can now read the paper.
:::

## With AI, the teacher has to be explicit {#prompts .lund-part .lund-sub data-part="4c"}

::: {.lund-prompts}
::: {.lund-card}
#### How to help (every problem)

```yaml
handwriting:
  language: English
  steps:
    - Level 1, find the mistake: point to it, do not give correct values.
    - Level 2, explanation: which law applies; no numbers, no final answer.
    - Level 3, method: numbered steps, stop before the numbers.
    - Level 4, worked solution.
```

The ladder keeps the struggle constructive: each click gives a little more help,
and the solution comes last.
:::

::: {.lund-card}
#### What to know (this problem)

```yaml
v25-1a:
  base-prompt: >-
    Reference: at the top the velocity is zero. t = v0/g = 0.61 s.
    The rise is v0²/(2g) = 1.83 m, so the height is 1.5 m + 1.83 m = 3.3 m.
    Typical mistakes: forgets the initial height; mixes up the signs of
    g and v0; answers only one of the questions; rounds too early.
```
:::
:::

[Shortened from the prompt files of the physics exercises. Teachers can try their own
changes in the prompt sandbox on the [physics exercises page](pages/handwriting-ai.qmd).]{.lund-small}

::: {.lund-big}
Teachers always knew this. Now it has to be **written down**.
:::

::::: {.lund-steps}
::: {.lund-step}
**The task**\
what the student sees
:::
::: {.lund-step}
**The check**\
decides whether the answer is right
:::
::: {.lund-step .lund-step-key}
**The prompt**\
the teacher's knowledge, written into the course
:::
:::::

## More practice, on request {#practice .lund-part data-part="5"}

::: {.lund-big}
Easier, similar, harder: the model writes new problems.
:::

::: {.lund-nest .lund-space}
::: {.lund-box .is-all}
**Everything a model can write**

::: {.lund-box .is-near}
**Near the course**

::: {.lund-box .is-ours}
**Written and checked by us**
:::
:::
:::
:::

::: {.lund-question}
Today the button asks the model directly; RAG can take its place and keep it near the course.
Still, we **give away control** in exchange for a **richer problem space**.
:::

::: {.lund-cols}
::: {.lund-card}
### Is it relevant?

- the teacher says what "harder" and "easier" mean
:::

::: {.lund-card}
### Is it solved correctly?

- computer algebra works out the answer where it can
- otherwise it is marked unverified
- it never counts toward grades
:::
:::

Try **Similar problem** on this exercise:

{{< include _includes/lund/derivative-course.md >}}

::: {.lund-question}
"Harder" is the model's reading of difficulty.
How it matches what **this** learner finds hard is an open question.
:::

## The point {#point .lund-part}

::: {.lund-takeaways}
- [0–1]{.lund-num} Model and prompt are settings. **The course** we have to define.
- [2]{.lund-num} **Let the model read the course**: inside first, outside clearly labelled.
- [3]{.lund-num} **Write it once, as plain text**: every view follows, many can work on it, no platform owns it.
- [4]{.lund-num} **The check decides** the answer, the AI helps; what teachers know must be **written down**.
- [5]{.lund-num} We **give away control** in exchange for a richer problem space.
:::

::: {.lund-big}
The course, written down, is the frame for productive AI.
:::
